name: AlertDialog
summary:
AlertDialog asks the user to confirm a destructive or irreversible action before it happens. Use it for things like deleting content, revoking access, or discarding unsaved changes.

It implements the WAI-ARIA APG [Alert Dialog pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alertdialog/): `role="alertdialog"`, a title linked by `aria-labelledby`, a consequence description linked by `aria-describedby`, focus moved into the dialog on open and returned to the trigger on close, and no dismissal by clicking outside. Escape cancels.

AlertDialog passes its requested width through to Dialog, which clamps the surface to the container and dynamic viewport with token gutters. Generic Dialog footers should wrap, but Dialog does not own action semantics or order; consumer composition controls that. AlertDialog owns its confirmation semantics: above 640px, actions render horizontally and may move onto another row; at 640px and below, the destructive action appears above Cancel and both buttons fill the footer width. Button labels retain their standard single-line behavior. The breakpoint follows available width, not pointer or hover capability. The body scrolls when block space is constrained.

On a touch screen the two actions are tracked as one group under a finger or a pen, the way iOS tracks the actions of an alert: the action under the finger highlights as soon as it is touched, the highlight follows the finger from one action to the other, and lifting the finger runs the action under it. Lifting it off both actions runs nothing. A mouse, the keyboard and assistive technology keep the click of each button.

Under a finger, on a phone or tablet, the alert also appears and leaves the way an iOS alert does: it scales down slightly into place while it and the dimming fade in, on the entrance timing of the theme, and it fades out with the dimming when it closes, on the exit timing of the theme. While it appears a touch does nothing (keys and assistive technology still act). While it leaves nothing reaches it: a touch, a click, a key or an assistive-technology activation does nothing, and a toast it raised stays live. With reduced motion it only cross-fades. With a mouse it keeps the theme entrance and closes at once.

For cases where you want to show an alert without managing open state, use the `useImperativeAlertDialog` hook: call `alert.show(options)` and render `alert.element` in your tree.

name: AppShell
summary: AppShell is the page shell for an application. It provides slots for top navigation, side navigation, banners, and main content. Use it as the root wrapper for every page. It handles responsive mobile navigation and skip-to-content automatically. Configure side nav collapse on SideNav with its collapsible prop.

name: AspectRatio
summary: Maintains a fixed width-to-height ratio for its children as its container resizes. Use it for media containers like videos, images, thumbnails, or any content that needs consistent proportions. It takes its width from the container and derives its height from the ratio, so it needs an ancestor with a definite width.

name: Avatar
summary: Avatar represents a person or team with a profile photo, initials, or a default icon. Use it in comment headers, contact lists, chat messages, user cards, and anywhere you need to identify someone visually.

name: AvatarGroup
summary: AvatarGroup displays multiple avatars in an overlapping row with an optional overflow indicator. Uses a compositional API: pass Avatar children directly so each avatar can carry its own props (status dots, click handlers, etc.).

name: AvatarGroupOverflow
summary: AvatarGroupOverflow appears at the end of an AvatarGroup to summarize people who are not shown individually. Use it when a group is sliced to a small number of visible avatars but the hidden count still matters.

name: AvatarStatusDot
summary: Size-aware status indicator dot that reads avatar size from context and scales proportionally. Each variant pairs a colour with a distinct built-in shape (filled, ring, minus) so status is never conveyed by colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1).

name: Badge
summary: Badge highlights a status or category at a glance. Use it sparingly: only when a value represents a distinct state (Active, Failed) or a grouping tag (Engineering, Design). Most metadata (dates, durations, counts, descriptions) should be plain description text, not badges.

name: Banner
summary: Banner shows a persistent message at the top of a page or section. Use it for form errors, system updates, maintenance notices, or success confirmations that the user needs to see until they act on it.

name: BaseTypeahead
summary: Composable combobox engine providing a bare input, search, keyboard navigation, and a styled result dropdown. It renders no input wrapper, border, or selected-value token. Typeahead and Tokenizer compose it for standard fields.

name: Blockquote
summary: A quotation block with a rule on its inline-start edge and secondary text color. Use to highlight quoted content, testimonials, or excerpts. The rule and padding are logical, so they move to the right edge in right-to-left locales.

name: BottomSheet
summary:
A mobile touch surface for filters, actions, forms, and detail views that should rise from the bottom of the viewport. For a multi-step flow, give each step its own sheet and one state value that names the open step (see Replacing a sheet); open a second sheet over the first when a step should stay visible beneath it.

Stacking. Every sheet keeps its own isOpen. Open a sheet while another scrim sheet is open and it stacks on top: the sheet beneath stays mounted with its scroll position and inputs, recedes behind the new one (the nearest covered sheet shrinks to 0.96 and lifts 8px, deeper ones to 0.92 and 16px), and is blocked from pointer, keyboard, and assistive technology by the top sheet's modal dialog. The sheets can be siblings, live in separate components, sit inside another sheet's content, or sit inside a BottomSheetSwitcher step; a whole switcher is one level, and switching its step in place does not change its position. Nothing moves in the DOM: each sheet's dialog stays where it is written, and no wrapper component is needed.

Order is open order. The top sheet is the one presented most recently that is still open; a sheet that closes and reopens comes back on top. When several sheets open in one update (a deep link into a flow), there is no open order between them, so tree order decides: a sheet below the sheets rendered in its content, siblings in the order they are written. That order is right in the first painted frame.

One scrim. Only the bottom sheet's backdrop dims the page; the backdrops of the sheets above it are transparent, so a stack never darkens per level. The dim holds steady while sheets push and pop, and if the bottom sheet closes while sheets remain above it, the next sheet's backdrop takes over in the same frame.

Dismissal. Escape, a tap on the scrim, a downward swipe, and a platform close request (Android back, a close watcher) reach only the top sheet, through that sheet's own onOpenChange, and that sheet's purpose applies: required blocks all of them, form blocks the scrim and the swipe. Nothing closes a whole stack at once; set every sheet closed in one update when a flow is done and they leave together.

Closing a covered sheet from code. Sheets rendered inside the closing sheet's content are part of it: they are presented only while it is open and leave with it. Their isOpen stays yours, as with a Dialog rendered in a closed Dialog: nothing is written to it, and a nested sheet that is still open when its host reopens is presented again, on top. Set it closed yourself when the flow is done. Sheets above the closing sheet that are not in its content stay open and keep their order; the closing sheet slides out from beneath them, and if it owned the scrim, the sheet above takes it over.

Replacing a sheet. Close the top sheet and open another in the same update (one state value that names the open step does this) and the new sheet replaces it instead of stacking on it: the new sheet rises above the one it replaces; if the replaced sheet is taller it moves down to meet the new sheet's top edge at the same time; the replaced sheet fades only after both motions finish, and is inert and hidden from assistive technology from the start. The scrim holds steady throughout, with no dip; focus moves into the new sheet; and when the flow closes, focus returns to the element that opened its first sheet, whichever sheet closed last. This is the handoff the deprecated BottomSheetSwitcher ran between its steps; a multi-step flow needs no switcher: give each step its own BottomSheet and one state value. A replace happens only when exactly one sheet closes and one opens in the update, the closing sheet was the top sheet of its stack, and the move was made from inside it (the control last pressed, or with no recent press the focused element, was in the closing sheet, as a step's own Continue or Back button is); a covered sheet closing while a sheet opens, a close and an open in different updates, or a close and an open driven from a control outside the closing sheet (two unrelated owners acting at once) keep the ordinary push and pop motion and their own focus return. A replace over an open stack runs one level up and leaves the sheets beneath covered. Non-modal sheets (hasScrim={false}) replace each other the same way, with no scrim: they are hosted in the browser top layer as manual popovers, so the entering step orders above the retained one with no page-level z-index, and toasts raised before or while the sheet is open stay above it. Below the Popover API support floor (Tier 2 in the browser support guide) the sheet falls back to show() in page stacking order: usable, but with no promise over later page content. A non-modal sheet returns focus to its opener on close only while focus is still inside it; focus taken elsewhere on the live page stays there.

Focus. Opening a sheet, modal or not, focuses its data-autofocus field (a TextInput with hasAutoFocus) in every browser. Without one, focus goes wherever the engine's native dialog focusing steps land: the panel in Chromium, and in Safari on iOS for a modal sheet; the first focusable control in Firefox. So to open on a field in every browser, mark it data-autofocus (a TextInput with hasAutoFocus). A step entering as a replacement also focuses a data-autofocus descendant first, so a flow that opens on a field keeps the keyboard on it. Closing the top sheet returns focus into the sheet it reveals: to the control that opened it when that control is still there, otherwise to the revealed sheet's panel. When the last sheet closes, the standalone rules apply: finalFocusRef, else the element that opened the sheet, with a focus ring only after keyboard input. When every sheet of a stack closes in one update, focus returns once, to the bottom sheet's finalFocusRef or opener, after the last dialog has closed.

Caveats. A Dialog, AlertDialog, or Popover opened from a sheet paints above the sheet and does not make it recede; a sheet opened from inside that Dialog paints above the Dialog and stacks over the sheet beneath. Sheets with hasScrim={false} stay out of the stack entirely (they replace each other, but never stack, recede, or take the scrim). A sheet React hides (a suspended Suspense boundary, Activity mode="hidden") leaves the stack and closes its dialog; when it is shown again it is presented again, on top. Only sheets rendered in the same document stack; a sheet inside an iframe is its own stack.

name: BottomSheetSwitcher
summary:
Deprecated: write each step as its own BottomSheet with isOpen, controlled by one state value that names the open step. Closing the top sheet and opening the next in the same update, from a control inside the open step, runs the same replace handoff (see BottomSheet, Replacing a sheet), with no sheetId and no switcher; a step changed from a control outside the flow (a page control, or code after focus left the step) closes and opens with ordinary push and pop motion. BottomSheetSwitcher keeps working until a future minor release removes it: a flow used on its own behaves as released (with three fixes: a toast raised from a step renders above the flow and can be pressed, under reduced motion its steps follow the reduced-motion rule, and a step with a hasAutoFocus field opens on that field in every browser), and a flow stacked with other sheets is one level of the stack (it recedes and is blocked when covered, shares the one scrim, and stands down from dismissal while covered). Modal and hasScrim={false} flows migrate the same way. Set activeSheet to a nested BottomSheet's sheetId to open or switch steps, and to null to close.

Stacking. A scrim flow is one level in the stack of open sheets (see BottomSheet, Stacking). Open it while a standalone sheet is open and the flow sits on top of that sheet, which recedes and is blocked; open a standalone sheet while the flow is open, from a step's content or from anywhere else, and that sheet sits on top while the whole flow recedes as one. Switching the step in place never changes the flow's position. Escape, the scrim, a swipe, and a platform close request reach only the top level: the flow's onActiveSheetChange(null) when the flow is on top, the standalone sheet's onOpenChange(false) when that sheet is. A standalone sheet rendered inside a step's content is presented only while that step is the active one: it leaves when the flow switches step or closes, its isOpen stays yours, and it is presented again, on top, if the step returns while it is still open. Only the bottom level's backdrop dims the page. A no-scrim flow stays out of the stack.

name: BreadcrumbItem
summary: BreadcrumbItem represents one destination, action, current location, or sibling-menu trigger inside a Breadcrumbs trail.

name: Breadcrumbs
summary: Breadcrumbs show a trail of links from the root to the current page. Use them at the top of detail pages, settings panels, or anywhere the user needs to see where they are and navigate back up.

name: Button
summary: Button triggers an action when clicked. Use it for form submissions, confirmations, navigation, or any interaction that needs a clear call to action.

name: ButtonGroup
summary: ButtonGroup joins related actions into a single connected control. Use it when multiple buttons represent related choices or operations that belong together visually, like copy/cut/paste, or undo/redo.

name: Calendar
summary: Calendar lets the user pick a date or date range from a month grid. Use it in booking flows, scheduling UIs, date filters, or anywhere the user needs to see surrounding dates for context.

name: Card
summary: Card is a bordered, elevated container for discrete, self-contained items: things you could reorder, remove, or interact with independently. Cards are NOT the default layout tool. Most content groups don't need a container at all; spacing and alignment create visual grouping naturally. Only reach for a Card when items need clear interaction boundaries or visual comparison in a grid.

name: Carousel
summary: Carousel scrolls a row of items horizontally when they overflow the available width. Use it for card grids, image galleries, product lists, or any set of items that should be browsable without taking up the full page.

name: Center
summary: Center aligns content to the middle of its container. Use it for empty states, loading screens, login forms, or any content that should sit in the center of the available space.

name: Chat
summary: Chat is a family of composable primitives for building AI and human chat experiences. Combine ChatLayout, ChatMessageList, ChatMessage, bubbles, system messages, tool calls, tokenized text, and ChatComposer to assemble complete conversations without reimplementing sender-aware layout, density, scrolling, or composer behavior.

name: ChatComposer
summary: ChatComposer is the message-entry shell for a chat surface. It coordinates a controlled or uncontrolled draft, provides a default token-capable input and send/stop action, and arranges optional drawer, header, footer, and status content. Custom inputs and send controls can join the same value, submission, disabled, stop, and focus contract through useChatComposerContext().

name: ChatComposerDrawer
summary: Use ChatComposerDrawer in the ChatComposer drawer slot for supplementary content such as attachments, context chips, or previews. Provide count only when people should be able to collapse that content.

name: ChatComposerInput
summary: Pass ChatComposerInput to ChatComposer's input slot when the draft needs trigger menus, inline tokens, history recall, dictation insertion, or file intake.

name: ChatComposerTokenElement
summary: Renders a single token chip outside the contentEditable input. Wraps a badge config or custom render function in the correct data-astryx-token span so the token serializes properly and stays visually consistent with tokens inside the composer.

name: ChatDictationButton
summary: ChatDictationButton is a toggle button that starts and stops voice dictation inside a chat composer. It pairs with useChatDictation to show a microphone icon when idle and animated frequency bars when listening. Place it in the sendActions slot of ChatComposer.

name: ChatLayout
summary: ChatLayout is the layout shell for full-page chat interfaces. It renders messages in normal page flow and docks the composer to the bottom with a frosted glass blur layer. Set the density prop to control spacing; it defaults to balanced. Use it to wrap ChatMessageList and ChatComposer for a complete chat experience with built-in auto-scroll and a scroll-to-bottom button.

name: ChatLayoutScrollButton
summary: Floating scroll-to-bottom button that appears when the user scrolls away from the latest messages. It fades in as a compact icon button and expands to show a label when new messages arrive. ChatLayout renders this by default: pass a custom element to the scrollButton prop to override, or null to hide it entirely.

name: ChatMessage
summary: Sender context wrapper: handles avatar, name, metadata, and alignment based on sender role.

name: ChatMessageBubble
summary: Styled content container for the chat "bubble." Reads sender from parent ChatMessage context to auto-style the background. Use filled for standard messages and ghost when content needs alignment without a visible boundary. Supports name/metadata slots aligned with bubble padding, and multi-bubble grouping via the group prop for consecutive messages from the same sender.

name: ChatMessageList
summary: Presentational message container with density context and infinite scroll support. Provides role="log" with aria-live="polite" for accessibility. A flex spacer pushes messages to the bottom when the list isn't full; set align="top" to start messages at the top instead.

name: ChatMessageMetadata
summary: Place ChatMessageMetadata below a message or in the last ChatMessageBubble metadata slot to show a timestamp, footer content, and optional delivery status. Non-rendering scalar slots (booleans and empty strings) create no separator; numeric zero remains visible. Composite React content remains caller-owned.

name: ChatSendButton
summary: Use ChatSendButton as ChatComposer’s send control when the action should switch between sending and stopping. Inside ChatComposer it reads readiness, streaming state, and action callbacks from context; standalone usage supplies those values explicitly.

name: ChatSystemMessage
summary: Use ChatSystemMessage for concise, non-sender content inside a chat transcript. Choose the default variant for factual status notices and the divider variant for date or section breaks. Long default content wraps within the available width. It carries no live role: inside a ChatMessageList, the log announces new notices. The divider branch includes a labelled separator.

name: ChatTokenizedText
summary: Use ChatTokenizedText inside a chat message when stored plain text contains serialized token values that should be projected as inline badges or caller-rendered token content. Unmatched text is preserved exactly and empty token values are ignored so rendering always finishes.

name: ChatToolCalls
summary: ChatToolCalls displays tool or function call invocations from an LLM response. Pass an array of calls and the component handles the rest: a single call renders inline, while multiple calls collapse into a summary with the latest call visible at the surface. Use it anywhere an AI agent shows what actions it took.

name: CheckboxInput
summary: CheckboxInput toggles a single on/off value. Use it for settings like "Enable notifications", terms acceptance, or opt-in choices. For multiple checkboxes in a group, use CheckboxList instead.

name: CheckboxList
summary: CheckboxList shows a small group of checkboxes so users can turn several options on or off at once. Place it in settings pages, filter panels, or forms where every choice should be visible without scrolling. For a single standalone checkbox (like "I agree to the terms"), use CheckboxInput instead. If only one option can be picked, use RadioList. If the list is long enough to need searching or scrolling, use MultiSelector instead.

name: CheckboxListItem
summary: Individual checkbox item with label, description, and end content slot. Works in collection mode (inside a CheckboxList with a value array) or standalone mode (inside List, or inside a CheckboxList without value, such as a select-all item). On a touch screen (a coarse primary pointer), a toggleable row is one press target: a touch on the label, the description or the box itself shows the pressed state on the row and its checkbox together. Where the primary pointer is fine, the box keeps its own press.

name: Citation
summary: Citations display inline references to external sources. Use them to attribute information within AI-generated responses, articles, or anywhere provenance and source links are needed.

name: ClickableCard
summary: An interactive card for navigation or action targets. Nested interactive elements work independently.

name: Code
summary: Code marks short inline references such as function names, variables, file paths, and command-line flags. Use CodeBlock for standalone or multi-line snippets.

name: CodeBlock
summary: CodeBlock renders syntax-highlighted code with line numbers, a copy button, and optional collapsible sections. Use CodeBlock for multi-line snippets like source files, terminal commands, and configuration examples. Use Code for inline references to function names, variables, or CLI flags within body text.

name: Collapsible
summary: Collapsible hides and reveals content behind a trigger button. Use it in settings panels, FAQ pages, or detail views to keep the page scannable while letting users drill into sections they care about. Wrap multiple collapsibles in CollapsibleGroup for accordion behavior. For custom collapsible components, use the `useCollapsible` hook directly (`astryx hook useCollapsible`).

name: CollapsibleGroup
summary: Coordinates multiple Collapsible instances so only one (single mode) or any number (multiple mode) can be open at a time. Renders no wrapper DOM element unless dividers are enabled.

name: CommandPalette
summary: CommandPalette is a searchable dialog for quick access to commands, navigation, and actions. Use it as a keyboard-driven launcher powered by SearchSource for filtering and selection.

name: CommandPaletteEmpty
summary: Empty state display for the results area. CommandPalette renders it automatically when a search returns no results, or when there is no query and bootstrap() returns nothing.

name: CommandPaletteFooter
summary: CommandPalette renders CommandPaletteFooter automatically. Pass a CommandPaletteFooter to the footer slot only when replacing the default guidance.

name: CommandPaletteGroup
summary: Visual grouping with a heading label. Place inside CommandPaletteList.

name: CommandPaletteInput
summary: Use CommandPaletteInput inside CommandPalette for a popup-backed command query, or as an independent search field when no result popup is present.

name: CommandPaletteItem
summary: Use CommandPaletteItem for one non-interactive result row inside CommandPaletteList or CommandPaletteGroup. CommandPalette owns the composite keyboard model; standalone items expose only their explicit visual state and pointer activation.

name: CommandPaletteList
summary: Scrollable results container. Renders as a listbox standalone, and inside CommandPalette while selectable results exist. Contains CommandPaletteItem and CommandPaletteGroup children.

name: ComplexSelector
summary: Use ComplexSelector when a selection needs richer custom content than a Selector option row. It is intentionally one component: ComplexSelector owns the field, trigger, popover, focus restore, and changeAction flow, while the content render prop owns the selector-specific accessible structure.

name: ContextMenu
summary: A right-click context menu that appears at the cursor position. Use to provide contextual actions for specific elements or regions without cluttering the UI with visible buttons.

name: ContextMenuItem
summary: Menu item component for compound mode. Re-exported from DropdownMenuItem for discoverability.

name: createAnimator
summary: Animates one element with the motion Astryx's own components use, without React. `animate` springs an element to new values on the state-change motion, `decay` flings it with the momentum of a released scroll view, and `set` moves it directly, so a card can follow a finger, snap back and be thrown away. Use the `useAnimator` hook in React. To animate an area's layout as its items change, use `useAnimatedLayout`; for what a component already animates, such as a sheet's detents or a carousel's snapping, use the component's own props.

name: createDragToSnapPoints
summary: Lets a drag move an element along one axis and settles it on snap points when the finger lifts, the way an iOS sheet settles on its detents: on the nearest snap point to where it is, on the next one in its direction after a quick flick, and back where it started when the finger was moving back. The settle continues the release's velocity. For a bottom sheet, use BottomSheet's `snapPoints`; for a scrolling row, Carousel's `hasSnap`. Use the `useDragToSnapPoints` hook in React.

name: createPanGesture
summary: Reports a drag on an element as values, without React, for a surface the product moves itself: a card that follows the finger, a drawer pulled by its handle. A finger, a mouse and a pen all drive it. A mouse or pen drag that starts on selectable text selects that text, and the pan reports nothing. Give that text `user-select: none`. The drag claims its touch at UIKit’s 10 pt, as `UIPanGestureRecognizer` does, so a tap stays a tap and a press or a long press is never reported as a pan. Use the `usePanGesture` hook in React. Where a component already offers the behavior, use its prop instead: BottomSheet's `snapPoints`, Carousel's `hasSnap`. Its example is on the usePanGesture page: one draggable box, made once with the hook and once with createPanGesture.

name: createReorderable
summary: Makes a collection's rows reorderable. On a touch screen a finger held still on a row's handle for a moment picks it up (a flick on the handle still scrolls): the row stays in its place, dimmed, while a copy of it follows the finger and an accent line marks where it would land; the other rows stay still, the page scrolls near its edges, and on release the rows rearrange. A pen held still on a handle where the primary pointer is coarse picks the row up as a finger does. A mouse, or a pen where the primary pointer is fine, drags a handle at once the same way, and the rows take their places without motion; a cancelled drag puts everything back at once. Without a drag, the handle toggles reorder mode for its row (a click, Space or Enter): each arrow key moves the row a place at once, and Escape or another activation ends the mode, keeping the moves; screen readers hear each move with the row's place and neighbours, and a hint shows the moves and Done as buttons, for taps alone. The reorder code ships with this function: a collection without the prop loads none of it.

name: createSwipe
summary: Gives a list row the verbs a sideways swipe uncovers, the way a mail row reveals Archive and Delete on a phone: `const mail = createSwipe({trailing: [{id: 'archive', label: 'Archive', onActivate: ({itemKey}) => archive(itemKey)}]})`, then `<ListItem label="Inbox" itemKey={message.id} swipe={mail} />`. A finger, a pen or a trackpad’s two-finger swipe drags the row; a mouse never does. A plain function, not a hook, pure and cheap: define the swipe once at module scope, where each handler reads the row from `itemKey`, or in `useMemo` when its handlers need component state. A new value with the same ids neither closes an open row nor restarts its settle, and it does no DOM work. The swipe’s code comes with this function, so a row given `swipe` is swipeable at its first paint and an app that never imports it ships none of it.

name: DateInput
summary: DateInput lets the user type or pick a date from a calendar popover. Use it for scheduling, deadlines, booking dates, or any form field that needs a specific calendar date.

name: DateRangeInput
summary: DateRangeInput lets users select a start and end date from a dual-month calendar popover. Use it for filtering data by time period, report generation, analytics dashboards, and booking flows.

name: DateTimeInput
summary: DateTimeInput combines date and time selection in one field. With presentation="adaptive-native" (the default), mouse/trackpad devices use Astryx typed fields and popovers, while coarse-pointer devices use browser/OS date and time controls in the same two-segment field. presentation="native" uses both native controls on every pointer; presentation="adaptive-bottom-sheet" keeps Astryx's own surfaces — pointer fields on fine pointers and the coordinated Date/Time bottom sheet on coarse pointers; "popover" and "bottom-sheet" force one Astryx surface on every pointer. The closed segments stay side by side when at least 400px is available and wrap into full-width rows below 400px, independent of viewport width. Use it for scheduling, event creation, deadline setting, or any form field that needs a specific datetime.

name: Dialog
summary:
Dialog displays a modal overlay that blocks interaction with the page until the user responds. Use it for delete confirmations, edit forms, terms acceptance, or any decision that should not be skipped.

For cases where you want to show a dialog without managing open state, use the `useImperativeDialog` hook: call `dialog.show(content)` and render `dialog.element` in your tree.

name: DialogHeader
summary: Use DialogHeader to give a dialog a labelled title area and optional close control.

name: Divider
summary: A visual separator that divides content into distinct sections. Use to create clear boundaries between groups of related content, or to demarcate interactive regions within a layout.

name: Drawer
summary:
A side panel that floats above page content for inspectors and detail views: the "click a table row, see its details" pattern. Unlike a docked panel it overlays the layout instead of reflowing it. Works on desktop and touch: the width budget applies on desktop and the panel preserves a 56px page reveal below 640px without exceeding the width budget. Escape closes the drawer (unless purpose is required) and focus returns to the element that opened it. Entry/exit slide animation respects prefers-reduced-motion. On a phone or tablet (a coarse primary pointer), a tap or a drag that lands while the drawer is still sliding in reaches nothing (for a drawer without a scrim, only one on the panel: the page stays live), and the drawer finishes sliding in; keys and assistive technology stay live, and a mouse or a trackpad still clicks: at once when it was the last pointer used, otherwise once it moves. Stacking contract: sibling drawers stack last-opened on top, Escape closes only the topmost, and closing peels innermost-first; render them as siblings, never nested.

Like Dialog, the drawer is a container: its content area is inset by --spacing-4 (16px) by default, by the padding prop, or by a theme's padding on drawer. Compose the header, body, and footer the way Dialog does, with a Layout: DrawerHeader in the header slot (it shows a close button when you pass it onOpenChange, like DialogHeader), the body in LayoutContent, and actions in LayoutFooter. The Layout redistributes the inset to those regions so they line up on one content line, and the header is not inset twice. A lone Section child also escapes the inset. Drawer renders no close button of its own, so give every drawer a visible way to close, especially a non-modal one, which has no scrim to click. Put data-autofocus on the control that should receive focus on open.

Choosing a surface: use Dialog for a centered decision or short form, Drawer for full-height side detail that keeps the page in sight, BottomSheet for block-axis sheets on touch, and a docked panel (a layout column) when content should reflow the page instead of floating over it.

Theming: the panel is the single stable target (astryx-drawer, with data-side reflecting side), and the scrim is the panel's native ::backdrop. DrawerHeader exposes astryx-drawer-header targets for its row, slots, and close icon.

name: DrawerHeader
summary: Compose DrawerHeader in the header slot of a Layout inside the Drawer, as DialogHeader is composed in Dialog, for a title row and, when you pass onOpenChange, a close button. The Layout keeps the header on the drawer inset instead of padding it twice. Drawer renders no close button of its own. Unlike DialogHeader it does not take focus on open (Drawer uses data-autofocus) and does not name the drawer (Drawer label does).

name: DropdownMenu
summary: A dropdown menu that displays a list of actionable items in a popup triggered by a button. Use to present action options as a next step in a process, or to offer contextual actions without cluttering the interface. Like the menus of macOS and iOS, the row under the pointer when it is released is the row that acts, the highlight follows a held mouse or finger, a mouse opens it on press and can drag straight into it, and a finger held on the trigger opens it with the finger down.

name: DropdownMenuCheckboxItem
summary: An independently checkable option inside DropdownMenu. The row owns menuitemcheckbox semantics while the shared Indicator supplies decorative checkbox paint.

name: DropdownMenuDivider
summary: A horizontal rule separating groups of rows in a compound menu. Renders role="separator", so it is never a stop in the arrow-key order. The data-driven equivalent is the `{type: "divider"}` entry in `items`; both modes render this component, so they look and theme identically. Host attributes and DOM handlers (id, data-*, aria-*) reach the separator; its role and orientation stay component-owned.

name: DropdownMenuGroup
summary: Use DropdownMenuGroup to give related compound-menu rows one visible and programmatic name. Use an untitled group only when a separate name would not help people understand the rows.

name: DropdownMenuItem
summary: Use DropdownMenuItem inside DropdownMenu compound mode for one action or destination. Keep label, description, icon, and endContent non-interactive; controls belong in separate rows or the menu header/footer.

name: DropdownMenuRadioGroup
summary: Use DropdownMenuRadioGroup inside compound-mode DropdownMenu when several commands represent one mutually exclusive choice. Keep value in caller state, provide a concise accessible label, and render each choice as DropdownMenuRadioItem.

name: DropdownMenuRadioItem
summary: A single option in a DropdownMenuRadioGroup (role="menuitemradio"). Must be used inside a DropdownMenuRadioGroup.

name: DropdownMenuSubMenu
summary: A single menu row that reveals a nested flyout of its own items. The row adopts DropdownMenuItem semantics (label / icon / description / isDisabled); its children become the flyout content. Opens inline-end with viewport auto-flip; Right/Enter/Space opens and focuses the first item, Left/Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger (Right/Left swap in RTL). On a phone (a coarse pointer, decided when the menu opened) the row drills in instead: its rows replace the menu's rows in the same box, led by a Back row named "Back to <parent>", and Back, Escape or ArrowLeft return to the row. Host attributes and DOM event handlers (aria-*, data-*, id) reach the trigger row, the element carrying role="menuitem" and aria-haspopup="menu"; a caller's handlers run after the row's own, except for the keys that open the flyout (the open arrow, Enter, Space) and a click on a disabled row. For data-driven menus, give a menu item a nested `items` array instead of using this component directly.

name: EmptyState
summary: EmptyState shows a placeholder when a content area has no data. Use it for empty lists, zero search results, first-time setups, or cleared inboxes. Always include a title and a next step so the user is not stuck.

name: Field
summary: Field is a low-level wrapper for custom, native, or third-party controls that do not already provide field label, description, and status UI. Use it when you need the Field shell around a control you own; use styled Astryx inputs like TextInput, Typeahead, and Select directly when they already expose label, description, and validation props.

name: FieldLabel
summary: Standalone label group for one control or a caller-labelled group, with optional supporting text, optionality indicators, icon, and tooltip.

name: FieldStatus
summary: FieldStatus renders validation feedback for fields and field-like controls. Use it directly for custom controls that need the same error, warning, or success presentation as Field.

name: FileInput
summary: FileInput provides file upload with optional drag-and-drop support. Use it for single or multiple file selection with built-in validation for file type, size, and count. Pair with validation status for upload feedback.

name: FormLayout
summary: A layout container that arranges form fields with consistent spacing and direction. FormLayout handles where fields go, not state or submission. Wrap it in a native <form> for that; <form> has no Astryx replacement, so it stays a plain element. Supports vertical (default), horizontal, and horizontal-labels directions, and can be nested to mix them.

name: Grid
summary: A CSS grid layout container for arranging children in rows and columns. Use Grid for card galleries, dashboards, and any multi-column layout. For columns that reflow on small screens, use `columns={{minWidth, max}}`; a numeric `columns` is exactly N columns at every width and never reflows.

name: GridSpan
summary: Grid item that spans multiple columns or rows.

name: Heading
summary: Semantic heading component that renders h1-h6 elements with themed styling, themed sizing via type scale tokens, and line-clamp truncation.

name: HoverCard
summary: HoverCard shows additional information when the user hovers or focuses a trigger element. Use it for profile cards, link summaries, or inline definitions where the user needs more context without navigating away.

name: Icon
summary: Icons are small visual symbols that represent actions, objects, or concepts. They improve scannability and reinforce meaning alongside text. Supports both direct SVG components and built-in meanings that adapt to the active theme.

name: IconButton
summary: A button that shows only an icon with no visible text. Use IconButton in toolbars, table rows, and compact UI where space is tight and the icon is universally understood.

name: Indicator
summary: Indicators are the componentized selection visuals shared by CheckboxInput, RadioList, and menu selection rows. They are decorative: the owning component keeps the input, role, accessible name, focus, and keyboard behavior, while the indicator turns state into a picture. That split is what makes them themeable: restyle one through its class targets, or replace the component outright.

name: InfoTip
summary: An info icon that reveals help: a small "i" button. Hover and keyboard focus preview the help, and a click, tap, Enter, or Space pins it open until Escape, a second press, a press outside, or focus leaving. Use it next to labels, values, and metrics for permission notes, metric definitions, and field help. Its value over hand-composing Icon inside Tooltip is the pre-wired accessible trigger: a real button with an aria-label, Tab-reachable, tooltip on hover AND focus AND tap, and Escape dismissal. It follows the toggletip pattern: the button reports `aria-expanded="true"` while the help is pinned, and a screen reader hears the help once when it pins. Host `data-*` attributes reach the button; its name and disclosure attributes stay component-owned.

name: InputGroup
summary: InputGroup connects an input with prefix/suffix addons in a single visual unit. Use it for URL fields, currency inputs, search fields with action buttons, or any input that needs contextual decorations.

name: InputGroupText
summary: Use InputGroupText inside InputGroup for a short fixed prefix or suffix, such as a currency symbol, a protocol, or a unit, or for a decorative icon. It is plain text, not a control, and it is not part of the input's accessible name.

name: InternationalizationProvider
summary: Wraps your app to set the active locale and (optionally) merge additional translation catalogs + per-locale overrides. Astryx components inside the subtree resolve their strings against this context. If no provider is present, components fall back to the shipped English defaults.

name: Item
summary: A single, flexible item primitive that unifies the "start content + label + description + end content" pattern across Astryx. Use it wherever you need a structured row: dropdown menus, selectors, contact lists, notifications, file browsers, and activity feeds.

name: Kbd
summary: Renders a keyboard shortcut as styled key badges. Use Kbd in menus and help text to show key combinations; in a Tooltip, write the shortcut as text.

name: Layer
summary: Layer utilities provide the app-level provider used by overlay systems. Use LayerProvider at the app root for toast/layer configuration; use higher-level Popover, HoverCard, or Tooltip APIs for most overlay UI. Rendered layer content, not the provider’s application subtree, uses theme body text defaults and exits ancestor surface/group membership. Establish intentional groups and complete required providers inside each layer. Every anchored layer keeps a gutter from each viewport edge — the spacing-4 step or the device safe-area inset, whichever is larger — and is capped to the viewport, never to the room beside its trigger: an explicit width renders at its size, flips when it does not fit beside the trigger, and slides into view when it fits on neither side. An app that floats a persistent bar over a viewport edge declares it once as inset on LayerProvider (blockStart, blockEnd, inlineStart, inlineEnd); each edge adds to that edge’s gutter for every anchored layer and moves the toast viewport by the same amount, and defaults to zero. The inset is app configuration, not a theme value.

name: Layout
summary: Layout is a general five-slot primitive for arranging header, start, content, end, and footer regions within a page or bounded container. AppShell owns the page shell and app-wide navigation behavior; use HStack or VStack for simple directional stacking.

name: LayoutContent
summary: Scrollable main content area.

name: LayoutFooter
summary: Bottom bar for action bars, pagination, and status bars.

name: LayoutHeader
summary: Top bar for page titles, app bars, and toolbars.

name: LayoutPanel
summary: Sidebar for navigation, settings, or inspector panels.

name: Lightbox
summary: A fullscreen overlay for viewing images and videos at full resolution. Supports single-item and gallery modes with prev/next navigation and swiping, optional zoom and pan for images, and native video controls.

name: Link
summary: A styled anchor for inline and standalone text navigation. Supports external links, underline variants, tooltips, and custom link components for router integration. Use it for navigating between pages or to external URLs.

name: LinkProvider
summary: Wraps your app to replace the default <a> tag with a framework-specific link component (e.g. Next.js Link) for client-side routing across all Astryx components.

name: List
summary: A vertical collection of items with consistent spacing, dividers, and optional markers. Supports headers, icons, avatars, badges, and interactive items with click or link behavior. Use it to display ordered or unordered groups of related content.

name: ListItem
summary: List item with label, description, start/end content slots, and interactive patterns.

name: Markdown
summary: Renders a markdown string as Astryx-styled components. Use Markdown for user-generated content, AI responses, and documentation; it handles headings, lists, tables, code blocks, and citations with consistent styling.

name: MediaTheme
summary: Provides token overrides for content rendered on inverted surfaces: media overlays, scrims, toasts, and tooltips. The base behavior flips color-scheme so all light-dark() tokens resolve to the correct side. Only a small set of tokens need explicit overrides beyond that. Themes can further customize component appearance on media surfaces via onDark/onLight in defineTheme(), with both token overrides (e.g. "--color-accent": "#90CAF9") and component overrides (e.g. ghost buttons get a border on dark surfaces).

name: MetadataList
summary: MetadataList displays key-value pairs for object attributes like quality, condition, and status, in a structured layout. Use it for detail panels, settings summaries, and record information.

name: MetadataListItem
summary: A single labeled metadata value within a MetadataList.

name: MobileNav
summary: A slide-out drawer for mobile navigation. MobileNav is the mobile counterpart to SideNav and accepts the same children. Use it on narrow viewports where a persistent sidebar is not practical. Inside AppShell, use MobileNavToggle as the trigger; it reads state from context automatically.

name: MoreMenu
summary: MoreMenu is a three-dot button that opens a list of actions. Use it for secondary actions that don't need to be always visible, like in table rows, card headers, or toolbars. Host `data-*` attributes reach the trigger button; its accessible name, `id`, and menu disclosure attributes stay component-owned.

name: MultiSelector
summary: A checkbox dropdown for selecting multiple values from a list. Selected items can display as a count, labels, or badges. Use it for filtering or when presenting a finite set of options where multiple choices are needed.

name: NavHeadingMenu
summary: Accessible menu container and items for nav heading popovers. NavHeadingMenu provides role="menu" with keyboard navigation; NavHeadingMenuItem renders individual selectable items. Pass as the menu prop of SideNavHeading or TopNavHeading.

name: NavIcon
summary: NavIcon is a circular icon container with an accent-colored background. Use it in navigation headers such as TopNavHeading and SideNavHeading to visually identify a section or application.

name: NumberInput
summary: A form input for numeric values with built-in validation, min/max constraints, and step controls. Use NumberInput for quantities, measurements, percentages, and similar inputs.

name: Outline
summary: A table-of-contents sidebar for documentation pages, help centers, wikis, and long settings pages. Use it for navigation within a single page, not for app routes. Features a sliding indicator track that animates to the active heading. Each link is in the normal Tab order, and Enter/Space activate.

name: OverflowList
summary: A horizontal list that automatically hides items when they exceed the available width. Use OverflowList for breadcrumbs, toolbars, tag lists, or any row that needs to collapse gracefully at smaller sizes.

name: Overlay
summary: Overlay layers action or supporting content over media, cards, video, or other bounded surfaces with an optional scrim and reveal behavior. Host attributes and DOM handlers (id, data-*, aria-*) reach the root element.

name: Pagination
summary: Pagination lets users step through pages of content. Place it below a table, list, or card grid so users can move forward and backward through results. Pick a variant to match the context: numbered pages for data tables, a count for large lists, compact for tight spaces, or dots for carousels.

name: Popover
summary: A click-triggered overlay anchored to a button or trigger element. Use it for secondary actions, inline confirmations, or supplementary information that does not warrant a full dialog. For hover previews use HoverCard, for brief helper text use Tooltip. Under a finger (a coarse primary pointer), it is presented like a native popover: it grows out of its trigger and shrinks back into it on the theme’s motion tokens; with reduced motion it cross-fades, opacity only, in 200 ms or less.

name: PowerSearch
summary: PowerSearch is a structured filter bar where each token represents a field, operator, and value. Use it for complex multi-dimensional filtering when users need to combine multiple search criteria. For simple single-field search, use a text input instead. Host `data-*` attributes, `data-testid` included, reach the primary control: the combobox input in the popover presentation and the trigger button in the sheet presentation. The `components.Token` and `components.Editor` defaults, `PowerSearchToken` and `PowerSearchFilterEditor`, pass them to the token and the editor root.

name: ProgressBar
summary: A horizontal bar showing the completion progress of a task. Use it for operations where the duration is known, or as an animated indicator when progress can't be calculated. Supports semantic color variants, value labels, and custom formatting. Under a finger a new value animates as on iOS: linearly, in proportion to how far it moves (a full track takes one second at the theme's default tempo), and the fill keeps a minimum visible length above zero.

name: RadioList
summary: A group of options where only one can be selected at a time. All options are visible at once, making it easy to compare choices. Use it when users need to pick one option from a small set.

name: RadioListItem
summary: Individual radio item with label, description, and content slots. Under a coarse pointer an enabled option’s target grows toward 44 px through an invisible hit area. It never shrinks below the row and stops at half the gap to a closer neighbour; the row keeps its size. That hit area is the row’s `::after`, so decorate a row with a child.

name: Resizable
summary: Hook-based resizable panel system. useResizable() manages size state and ResizeHandle provides the interactive pill-grip separator. Pass the hook's output to existing layout components via their resizable prop.

name: ScrollableArea
summary: Provides a native scroll viewport and a real observed content box. The viewport enters the tab order only while a requested logical axis is effectively scrollable, and containment applies only to effective axes.

name: Section
summary: Section is the correct way to create page regions and group related content on a page. Use it for settings groups, form sections, sidebar areas, or any time you need visual separation between parts of a page. If you are tempted to use a Card for a page section, use Section instead.

name: SegmentedControl
summary: A segmented button group that allows users to make a single selection from a small set of mutually exclusive options. Use SegmentedControl when all options should be visible at once and the selection controls a value or mode, not page navigation. Under a finger, on a touch device (a coarse primary pointer), the selection slides to the new segment, whether a tap, an arrow key or a new value moved it; with Reduce Motion nothing travels: the old selection fades out as the new one fades in. There, pressing the selected segment lifts it, and dragging it carries the selection along with the selected label’s colour following it, and the segment under the finger is chosen when it lets go; a tap selects through the browser’s click; a pressed unselected segment shows the shared pressed overlay, and nothing dims. A drag that drifts off the control still chooses by its position along it. Going back to the selected segment, or Escape, changes nothing. With a mouse or a pen every change, a click included, slides on the theme’s duration and easing, and dragging the selected segment carries it as a finger does.

name: SegmentedControlItem
summary: Individual segment item rendering as a radio button within the segmented control.

name: SelectableCard
summary: A card that toggles between selected and unselected states with an accent border. For navigation use ClickableCard.

name: Selector
summary: A dropdown selector for choosing a single value from a list of options. Supports labels, validation, descriptions, and required/optional states. Use it in forms and settings when presenting a moderate number of options. Keyboard typeahead matches a native select: typing on the focused closed trigger selects the matching option directly, repeated presses cycle through options sharing a first letter, and spaces count as match characters ("new y" reaches "New York"). With the menu open, typing moves the highlight and Enter commits. With hasSearch, typing on the closed trigger opens the popup and seeds the search input.

name: SelectorOption
summary: Helper component for custom item rendering inside an Selector renderOption prop.

name: SideNav
summary: A sidebar navigation component for organizing application pages with sections, nested items, and icons. Use SideNav as the primary navigation when an app has 5 or more destinations or requires hierarchical grouping.

name: SideNavCollapseButton
summary: Toggle button for sidenav collapse. Place inside SideNav (reads context automatically) or outside it (hand the same controlled collapsible config to both). Renders as an icon-only ghost button by default.

name: SideNavHeading
summary: Product/suite/account heading with smart interaction boundary logic for links and a menu popover.

name: SideNavItem
summary: Navigation item with icon, selected state, optional end content, and nesting support via children.

name: SideNavSection
summary: Section grouping with an optional title, subtitle, and end content.

name: Skeleton
summary: An animated shimmer placeholder that previews the shape of content while it loads. Use it to build loading screens that match the layout of the real content. For content with unknown dimensions, use Spinner instead.

name: Slider
summary: A draggable control for selecting a numeric value or range within defined bounds. Supports single value and range selection, tick marks, custom value formatting, and vertical orientation. Use it when users need to explore a continuous range, such as volume, price, or percentage. Under a finger, on any touch device, it tracks as UISlider does: only the thumb takes a drag, through a target larger than it, the value follows the finger’s travel rather than jumping to it, a release coasts on before `onChangeEnd`, a swipe from the track scrolls the page, and a tap on the track or a mark sets the value when the finger lifts (the thumb springs there). A mouse drag on a thumb tracks the same way, past the same 10 px in any direction, with no lift or coast; a mouse press on the track moves the thumb there, and only a primary click presses. A pen drags as a finger does, claiming only along the track, and its drag ends at the release with no coast. A wheel or a trackpad scroll over the slider goes to whatever scrolls under it.

name: Spinner
summary: An animated loading indicator for processes with unknown duration, such as data fetching or form submission. Supports visible labels, multiple sizes, and a dark background variant. For content with known dimensions, use Skeleton instead.

name: Stack
summary: Stack arranges items in a row or column with consistent spacing. Use the gap prop to control the space between items.

name: StatusDot
summary: A small colored dot that communicates status like online/offline presence or severity levels. Supports five semantic variants and an optional pulse animation. Always pair with a visible text label, as color alone should not carry meaning.

name: Step
summary: Individual step within a Stepper. Renders a progress-bar segment, an indicator, and a label with optional description. Progress (completed/active/not-started) is derived from the parent Stepper's activeStep and this step's step index.

name: Stepper
summary: Steppers display progress through a sequence of logical and numbered steps. Use them for multi-step workflows like forms, onboarding flows, or checkout processes where users need to see their position and the steps ahead. Rendered as an ordered list (not a navigation landmark).

name: Switch
summary: A toggle control for on/off states that take effect immediately. Supports labels, descriptions, loading states, and validation. Use it for settings or preferences that apply instantly. For changes requiring a form submission, use a checkbox instead. Under a finger it moves like the iOS switch on every touch screen: a press lifts the thumb, a drag across flips it, lifting the finger commits, and a tap toggles through the browser’s click. The thumb keeps its circle and size on every device, and under a coarse pointer the invisible hit area grows toward 44 × 44 px, stopping halfway to any neighbouring control so a tap goes to the nearer one. With reduced motion on, a change cross-fades on a touch screen and is immediate with a mouse.

name: SyntaxTheme
summary: Applies syntax highlighting colors to CodeBlock and any code component in the subtree. By default, code components use the theme-level syntax colors (set via defineTheme({ syntax: ... })), which derive from the palette (--color-text-accent for keywords, --color-text-green for strings, etc.). SyntaxTheme lets you override those per-region. The system uses 14 semantic tokens (keyword, string, comment, number, function, type, variable, operator, constant, tag, attribute, property, punctuation, background) validated against 11 community themes. Custom themes are created with defineSyntaxTheme() and can use [light, dark] tuples for automatic color-scheme adaptation. Built-in presets: oneDarkPro, dracula, monokai, nord, tokyoNight, catppuccinMocha, githubLight, githubDark, solarizedLight, oneLight (import from @astryxdesign/core/theme/syntax).

name: Tab
summary: Individual tab item that renders as a button or an anchor link, with selected-state styling and optional icons.

name: Table
summary: Table displays structured data in rows and columns with consistent dimensionality. It supports rich cell content, sorting, selection, pagination, and column management through a composable plugin system. Use Table for data sets with uniform structure; for simpler or inconsistent data, consider a list or card layout instead.

name: TableBody
summary: <tbody> wrapper for children mode. Holds the data rows. A row must sit inside a section: <table> cannot contain a <tr> directly, because the HTML parser inserts an implied <tbody> when it parses server-rendered markup and React does not when it renders on the client, so rows written straight into Table mismatch on hydration. The data-driven data={...} mode renders this element itself; in children mode it is yours to supply.

name: TableCell
summary: <td> wrapper that reads TableContext to apply density padding, font size, and divider borders when used inside Table.

name: TableFooter
summary: <tfoot> wrapper for children mode. Holds summary or total rows beneath the body. A row must sit inside a section: <table> cannot contain a <tr> directly, because the HTML parser inserts an implied <tbody> when it parses server-rendered markup and React does not when it renders on the client, so the two trees mismatch on hydration. Children mode only: the data-driven data={...} path renders a header and a body, never a footer.

name: TableHeader
summary: <thead> wrapper for children mode. Holds the header row, whose cells are TableHeaderCell. A row must sit inside a section: <table> cannot contain a <tr> directly, because the HTML parser inserts an implied <tbody> when it parses server-rendered markup and React does not when it renders on the client, so the two trees mismatch on hydration. The data-driven data={...} mode renders this element itself whenever columns are supplied; in children mode it is yours to supply.

name: TableHeaderCell
summary: <th> wrapper that reads TableContext to apply density padding, semibold weight, secondary text color, and divider borders when used inside Table.

name: TableRow
summary: <tr> wrapper that reads TableContext to apply striped, hover, and divider styles when used inside Table.

name: TableSelectionToolbar
summary: Pass both outputs of useTableSelectionState to their matching consumers: selectionConfig to useTableSelection and selectionState to TableSelectionToolbar. An app that keeps its own selection, such as every row matching a query across server pages, passes its own config and state instead. Render product actions through startContent. Keep fixed or floating placement in the surrounding layout.

name: TabList
summary: TabList provides tab-style navigation for organizing content into categorized sections. Use it to let users switch between related views without leaving the page. A strip narrower than its tabs scrolls horizontally and keeps the selected tab in view.

name: TabMenu
summary: Overflow menu trigger that opens a dropdown of additional tab options, showing the selected option's label as the trigger text. Host attributes and DOM event handlers (id, aria-*, data-*, drag and drop) reach the trigger button, not the popup or its options. The button keeps its role, tab stop, and menu disclosure attributes.

name: Text
summary: Text renders styled body text and headings from the theme. Use Text with a semantic type for body copy, labels, and captions, and Heading for section titles that output the correct h1–h6 element.

name: TextArea
summary: TextArea is a multi-line text input for collecting longer-form content like comments, descriptions, or messages. Use it when the expected input spans multiple lines. For shorter, single-line values, use TextInput.

name: TextInput
summary: TextInput collects short-form text like names, emails, or search queries. Use it for single-line values where the expected input is brief. Pair it with validation status to guide users through required or formatted fields.

name: Theme
Thumbnail
summary: Thumbnail displays a compact, square preview of an image attachment. It shows a shimmer effect while uploading, the image on success, and a placeholder icon when no source is set. Use it in chat composers, file upload lists, or anywhere you need a small image preview with optional remove and click actions.

name: TimeInput
summary: TimeInput uses a browser/OS time picker on coarse pointers by default and Astryx's typed field on fine pointers. It converts values to a standard format and supports arrow-key adjustment on the typed surface. Use it in forms, scheduling flows, or any interface where users need to select a specific time.

name: Timer
summary: Displays a standardized elapsed duration for active work without scheduling a React render on every tick. Elapsed format updates by second below one hour and by minute after one hour; clock format remains second-precise.

name: Timestamp
summary: Timestamp formats a date or time value into human-readable text. Use it to show when something was created, updated, or is scheduled; picking relative for recency, absolute for precision, or auto to let the component decide.

name: Toast
summary:
Toast shows a brief, non-blocking notification to confirm an action or present temporary information; show one with `const showToast = useToast()`, which needs no provider or mounted ToastViewport: inside LayerProvider (or a ToastViewport) it uses that viewport, and otherwise the first toast mounts a fallback viewport on document.body with a development warning. Use it for scenarios where the user needs feedback but not a decision, such as saving, deleting, or changing a status.

For production use, prefer the `useToast()` hook; it handles positioning, stacking, auto-dismiss, and deduplication via `ToastViewport`. Only the viewport announces a toast: a `Toast` rendered on its own, as in a preview, is not a live region and announces nothing. Toasts stay within viewport and safe-area gutters, wrap long message content, and enter, exit, or swipe-dismiss toward their configured top or bottom edge. The vertical swipe uses the same spatial model as placement motion: top Toasts leave upward and bottom Toasts leave downward. Swipe waits for dominant edge-directed intent before cancelling native touch movement and reports the existing manual dismissal reason. Pen is supported as direct-contact input; mouse drag is excluded to avoid conflicting with desktop text selection, where the visible close control remains available. Set `isAutoHide: false` explicitly when an action or message must remain available. The `Toast` component renders the visual toast element inline and is useful for previews, documentation, and static showcases where the viewport lifecycle is not needed. Host `data-*` attributes on `Toast` reach the toast element; its role, live-region attributes, and theme attributes stay component-owned.

name: ToggleButton
summary: ToggleButton switches between selected and unselected states to represent a persistent on/off choice. Use it standalone for binary actions like bold, mute, or favorite, or inside a ToggleButtonGroup for single-select or multi-select toolbar controls.

name: ToggleButtonGroup
summary: Groups toggle buttons for exclusive (single) or multi-select behavior. Uses discriminated union on type for type-safe value/onChange. Under the touch presentation a press tracks like a menu: press a toggle and slide across the others, and the highlight follows. Only the toggle you lift on toggles, and lifting outside the group toggles nothing. With a finger, each toggle's target grows toward 44 px, up to half the gap to a neighbour, without the toggles growing.

name: Token
summary: Token is a small, inline element for representing discrete pieces of associated data, like tags, categories, or selections. Use it to label content, show active filters, or represent removable items like selected recipients in a compose field.

name: Tokenizer
summary: Tokenizer is a multi-select input that lets users search, select, and manage multiple items displayed as removable chips. Use it when users need to build a set of selections from a searchable data source, like adding team members, applying tags, or choosing filters.

name: Toolbar
summary: Toolbar is a horizontal bar with left, center, and right areas. Use it for contextual actions within a content area (above a table, inside a card, or in a panel), not as a page-level header. Set the size once on the toolbar and all buttons, inputs, and tabs inside it match automatically.

name: Tooltip
summary: A short text hint that appears on hover or focus, anchored to a trigger element. Use it to describe icon-only buttons, show the full text of truncated labels, or provide supplementary context without cluttering the UI.

name: TopNav
summary: TopNav is a horizontal navigation bar for product-level navigation in application headers. Use TopNav for 5 or fewer always-visible navigation items, or minimal navigation paired with search and controls. For complex navigation hierarchies, use a sidebar; to filter content, use tabs or filter buttons instead.

name: TopNavHeading
summary: Product/suite/account heading for the TopNav heading slot. Supports smart interaction boundary logic: logo, heading text, superheading/subheading with independent links, and an optional menu popover with automatic chevron indicator.

name: TopNavItem
summary: Navigation link item for use in TopNav startContent: renders as an anchor with hover and selected states.

name: TopNavMegaMenu
summary: Navigation item that displays a full-width mega menu panel on hover. Uses a slots API with items and featured props. TopNavMegaMenuItem renders itself in both desktop and mobile drawer modes. Supports inline collapsible drawer via render mode context.

name: TopNavMegaMenuFeaturedCard
summary: Standard featured card for the TopNavMegaMenu featured slot. Provides a consistent card with optional image, title, description, and CTA link.

name: TopNavMegaMenuItem
summary: An individual item inside an TopNavMegaMenu. Renders itself in both desktop (popover grid) and mobile drawer modes via render mode context.

name: TopNavMenu
summary: Navigation item that displays a hover-triggered popover menu with rich items containing an icon, title, and optional description.

name: TreeList
summary: An expandable tree structure for displaying hierarchical data with branch connector lines. Use it for file explorers, nested category browsers, or any interface that visualizes parent-child relationships. Under a finger, expanding a row glides the rows below it while its children fade in on the same timing, and a collapse plays it back; pass an `animatedLayout` handle for content after the tree to glide too.

name: Typeahead
summary: A searchable input for selecting a single item from a large or dynamic dataset. Results appear as the user types, with support for async data sources, debounced search, and custom item rendering. Use it when the option list is too large for a Selector dropdown.

name: TypeaheadItem
summary: Default dropdown item renderer for typeahead results. Shows label with optional icon, description, and avatar. Exported for use in custom renderItem implementations.

name: useAnimatedLayout
summary: Returns a handle to pass to a component whose size changes, such as TreeList or Collapsible. When that component changes size, it and the content after it inside `containerRef` animate together on one shared motion role. Fixed and stuck sticky elements stay put, the glide never scrolls the area, and Reduce Motion is respected. It applies under every pointer, a mouse included. Without the handle a component keeps its jump: content after it takes its place at once. Content after the change may mix Astryx components and your own elements; none of it opts in.

name: useAnimator
summary: Animates one element with the motion Astryx's own components use. Call `animator.animate` to spring an element to new values on the state-change motion, `animator.decay` to fling it with the momentum of a released scroll view, and `animator.set` to move it directly, so a card can follow a finger, snap back and be thrown away. To animate an area's layout as its items change, use `useAnimatedLayout`; for what a component already animates, such as a sheet's detents or a carousel's snapping, use the component's own props. Outside React, use `createAnimator`.

name: useAnnounce
summary: Imperatively announces a message to screen readers through a visually-hidden live region. Use it for state that is only conveyed visually; search result counts, "no results", loading and saved confirmations, validation errors (WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages). The polite and assertive regions are created empty on first use and stay mounted, which is what makes announcements reliable: most screen readers ignore a live region that is inserted together with its content. Each message is cleared a couple of seconds after it is announced so stale status does not linger in the accessibility tree. A message is delivered where its caller is: from inside an open Astryx modal it goes to a region inside that modal and is heard there with no change to the calling code; a message sent just as the modal is dismissed is delivered through whatever is exposed afterwards rather than lost. A call made outside the modal, even by the component that renders it, uses the page-body region.

name: useAppShellMobile
summary: Hook for reading and controlling AppShell mobile navigation state from descendants of AppShell. Use it for custom mobile nav triggers, closing the drawer after route changes, or coordinating AppShell-adjacent mobile experiences with the same breakpoint used by mobile nav.

name: useCalendarConstraints
summary: Provides date constraint validation for calendar views and custom range pickers. It combines boundary dates, span limits measured from an in-progress range start, and custom rules (such as weekly closures or blackout dates) into an isDateDisabled predicate. Calendar uses it internally to disable day buttons; use it directly when building bespoke scheduling interfaces or range pickers.

name: useCalendarDays
summary: Builds the day grid for one month: every date to show, including the previous and next months' days that fill the first and last weeks, grouped into weeks, plus localized weekday header names that start on weekStartsOn. It is the layout Calendar uses, for a custom month view such as a compact availability grid or a mini calendar. It returns data only: rendering, selection, keyboard navigation and the grid's accessibility semantics are the caller's.

name: useCalendarNavigation
summary: Manages visible month state and pagination for calendar components. It provides previous/next month stepping, localized month-year header strings, and pending focus tracking so keyboard arrow navigation seamlessly moves focus across month boundaries into the adjacent month. Use it directly when composing custom calendar headers, pager controls, or dual-month availability pickers.

name: useChatDictation
summary: Voice input for a chat composer. It wraps speech recognition with microphone level, start and stop cues, and optional interim text in a ChatComposerInput. Check isSupported before offering the control. A browser without speech recognition reports false and does not listen. Sustained loud speech turns the transcript to upper case.

name: useChatPasteAsToken
summary: Turns a long plain-text paste into a token chip in a ChatComposerInput. Short pastes are left for the composer to insert. Pass the returned object as pasteAsToken. The default threshold is 200 characters.

name: useClickableContainer
summary: Makes a container element clickable while preserving nested interactive element behavior. Solves the "nested interactive elements" problem: when a card is clickable but contains buttons/links, clicking those should NOT trigger the card's action. Detects interactive ancestors between the click target and the container, and ignores text selections. Supports href navigation (including middle-click and Ctrl/Cmd+click for new tabs).

name: useClipboard
summary: Copy-to-clipboard behavior: the clipboard write, a transient isCopied flag with its own reset timer, and an optional polite screen-reader announcement. Extracted so every copy affordance is a thin control over one implementation instead of re-deriving the timer and announcement. Rapid re-copies restart the reset timer so the confirmation always lasts the full duration, and the timer is cleaned up on unmount. It also copies inside a sandboxed frame that refuses the async Clipboard API, with the browser copy command, inside the reader’s click or key press. CodeBlock and Timestamp build their built-in copy buttons on it; reach for it directly when building a copy affordance that is not a plain icon button (a menu item, a labeled text button, a copy-on-click value chip).

name: useCollapsible
summary: Reusable hook that encapsulates the collapsible state machine. Supports three modes: group-controlled (inside CollapsibleGroup), controlled (isOpen + onOpenChange), and uncontrolled (self-managed with defaultIsOpen). Used internally by Card and Section.

name: useCollator
summary: Returns the sanctioned locale-aware comparator for custom sorting. The collator is recreated when the provider locale or an option changes.

name: useCombobox
summary: Tracks the active option of a single-select combobox and handles its keys, while DOM focus stays on the control. It powers Selector and CommandPalette; use it to build a combobox those components do not cover, including one over a single-line text field you render yourself, such as a search field whose results replace a page section, or an “add people” field in a dialog. It renders nothing: you render the field, the listbox and the options, and spread `getFieldProps`, `getListboxProps` and `getOptionProps` onto them, or wire `role`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant` yourself from `onKeyDown` and `getItemId` for a control such as a button.

name: useContainerReveal
summary: A headless hover/focus reveal primitive. Gives a container a scoped trigger that reveals (or conceals) content inside it when the container is hovered or receives keyboard focus: the classic "row actions appear on hover" pattern. The reveal is CSS-only: no hover state lives in React and hovering never triggers a re-render. The caller authors no StyleX for the reveal itself; the hook hands out the container and content styles, and a nested container shadows its ancestor, so nested containers never leak hover/focus into one another. Accessible by construction: revealed content is visually hidden at rest with position and opacity (never display:none), so it stays mounted, keeps its place in the tab order, and is announced to assistive technology; it reveals on :focus-within so keyboard users see it when tabbing in, stays visible under a coarse primary pointer (never gated behind hover there), and honors prefers-reduced-motion.

name: useDevWarning
summary: Fires a dev-only "Component: message" console warning once per mount while the condition holds. It is the render-safe way for a component to flag misuse: warning straight from the render body repeats on every render, and gating it with state adds a re-render, so this uses a ref and an effect instead. For a warning outside a component, use the imperative devWarn utility.

name: useDirection
summary: Reads the current text direction during render. Reach for this hook as a last resort when render-time direction is strictly required (such as canvas drawing that cannot use CSS logical properties). In order of preference, always favor: CSS logical properties (margin-inline, inset-inline); shared mirror styles for directional icons (CSS scaleX); and DOM reads for keyboard or gesture logic.

name: useDragToSnapPoints
summary: Lets a drag move an element along one axis and settles it on snap points when the finger lifts, the way an iOS sheet settles on its detents: on the nearest snap point to where it is, on the next one in its direction after a quick flick, and back where it started when the finger was moving back. The settle continues the release's velocity. For a bottom sheet, use BottomSheet's `snapPoints`; for a scrolling row, Carousel's `hasSnap`. Outside React, use `createDragToSnapPoints`.

name: useEntryAnimation
summary: Returns a StyleX style for animating an element on mount.
