Only animates when the element is dynamically inserted after the initial page paint; elements rendered on page load are not animated. Uses Astryx motion tokens (duration, easing) for consistent animation timing. Server-rendered elements hydrate without the entry style and never animate; elements mounted after hydration animate.

name: useFocusTrap
summary: Traps focus within a container element following the WAI-ARIA dialog focus trap pattern. Listens to focus events on the document and redirects focus back into the container if a Tab from inside it moves focus out. Handles both Tab and Shift+Tab wrapping. A Tab pressed while focus is outside the container is left to the page, so an open non-modal surface never takes over the focus order of the page. When the trap deactivates or unmounts, focus is restored to the element that was focused before activation, unless focus was already moved elsewhere or never entered the trap (so popups that keep focus on their trigger, like comboboxes, are unaffected). Mouse clicks outside the container are not intercepted; use a light-dismiss handler for that.

name: useGridFocus
summary: Manages keyboard navigation within a 2D grid following the WAI-ARIA grid pattern. Supports arrow keys for cell-to-cell navigation, Home/End for row boundaries, Ctrl+Home/Ctrl+End for grid boundaries, and Page Up/Down for custom callbacks (e.g., month navigation in calendars). Boundary navigation callbacks allow cross-grid navigation.

name: useHotkeys
summary: Registers global keyboard shortcuts with a single window keydown listener per hook instance. Handlers live in a ref, so re-renders never re-subscribe. Skips events from typing targets (input, textarea, select, contenteditable) unless allowInInputs, skips defaultPrevented events, and calls preventDefault() on match. SSR-safe.

name: useHoverCard
summary: Headless hook for hover-triggered floating cards. Builds on useLayer with hover/focus intent detection, configurable delays, safe hover behavior, and accessible aria-describedby linking. Use for rich previews on hover when you need full control over the trigger or rendered content.

name: useIcon
summary: Resolves a built-in meaning to a React node through the nearest Theme, so a custom component draws the same success, warning or error icon that Astryx components draw and follows a theme that overrides it. Resolution reads the nearest Theme's icons (outside any Theme, the registered theme the document root names), then registerIcons() overrides, then the built-in default. The node is returned as is, with no size or color wrapper: the built-in icons are 1em squares in currentColor, so they follow the surrounding text. A function entry is read at {size: 'md'}. Render <Icon icon={name} /> instead when the icon needs another size, a color or a label.

name: useImageMode
summary: Detects whether an image is predominantly dark or light by sampling pixels via OffscreenCanvas. Uses APCA perceptual lightness (sRGB linearization + power curve) for accurate detection, especially on saturated colors. Runs entirely off the paint path: no visible canvas, no layout thrash. Supports regional sampling for detecting luminance where text overlays will appear. Returns null while loading and falls back gracefully on CORS or network errors.

name: useImperativeAlertDialog
summary: Hook for showing an alert dialog without managing open state. Call alert.show(options) to open and alert.hide() to close. Render alert.element in your JSX tree.

name: useImperativeDialog
summary: Hook for showing a dialog without managing open state. Call dialog.show(content, options) to open and dialog.hide() to close. Render dialog.element in your JSX tree.

name: useIndicatorFocusRing
summary: Draws the standard focus ring on the indicator of a control whose real input is visually hidden; a checkbox or radio focuses an opacity-0 input, so the ring has to appear on the picture beside it. The ring is painted imperatively on the indicator's own element, which is the only element whose border-radius can shape it, and only on :focus-visible, so pointer clicks stay quiet. Owning it here means a theme-supplied indicator cannot ship a control with no visible focus (WCAG 2.4.7) by ignoring a prop.

name: useInputContainer
summary: Makes an input container wrapper clickable, delegating focus to the inner input/textarea when the user clicks non-interactive areas (icons, padding, status indicators). Built on top of useClickableContainer, so nested interactive elements (clear buttons, calendar toggles, links) are handled safely; clicking them does NOT steal focus from the input. Automatically detects input type: text-like inputs receive .focus(), while other types (checkbox, radio, file) receive .click().

name: useInputStatusIcon
summary: Builds the on-field status affordance for a bordered input and its accessibility wiring, so every input in the family behaves the same for a given status. The attached variant renders a plain glyph and leaves the text to the message box; the detached variant renders nothing here, because the message box already carries its own icon; the tooltip variant renders a real focusable button whose tooltip is reachable by keyboard, pointer, touch and assistive tech. Use it when building a bordered input, not for field-level messaging.

name: useInteractiveRole
summary: Resolves what a polymorphic component should render as, in one place: href wins, then onClick, then an interactive trigger context supplied by a parent (Popover, DropdownMenu and friends), then inert. Use it in any component that is sometimes a link, sometimes a button, and sometimes plain content; Token, Thumbnail, Item and ClickableCard all do. Because context is part of the resolution, a component built on it becomes a valid trigger for new surfaces without changing.

name: useKeyboardHint
summary: Shows an ephemeral "← → to navigate" hint anchored to the focused item the first time a roving-tabindex composite (Toolbar, TabList, SegmentedControl, etc.) receives keyboard focus. It teaches sighted keyboard users that arrow keys move within the group. The hint renders arrow keys with Kbd in the top layer (popover="manual") and is CSS-anchor-positioned to the focused element, so overflow containers never clip it. It stays until the first arrow press, Escape, or blur, and does not re-show for that instance. Escape closes only the hint, through the shared layer dismissal stack, and keeps focus where it is. Toolbar, TabList, and SegmentedControl wire this in automatically; reach for the hook directly only when building a custom roving-tabindex widget.

name: useLayer
summary: Core positioning hook for rendering overlay content using CSS Anchor Positioning and the Popover API. Use it as the foundation for custom popovers, hover cards, tooltips, and fixed-position layers when higher-level components are not enough. Both modes use theme body text defaults and end ancestor surface/group membership as a whole, including group-owned state. Explicit props and unrelated contexts remain unchanged. Apply intentional formatting through render styles or content, and establish complete content-local providers inside the rendered layer.

name: useLightbox
summary: State management and accessible trigger wiring for Lightbox. Eliminates boilerplate for managing open state and current index. Returns trigger props with button role, tabIndex={0}, aria-haspopup="dialog", and keyboard activation handlers, along with a pre-wired Lightbox element that handles dismissal, next/previous navigation, and focus restoration.

name: useLinkComponent
summary: Resolves which component renders a link, so a custom component's links follow the app's router the same way Astryx's own links do. The order is the as argument, then the nearest LinkProvider's component, then a native anchor. Render the returned component with href (and to, for a router that reads it). Before rendering it checks both destinations under the Link href rule: a rejected destination renders an anchor with no destination, and a custom router is never invoked with it. A custom component receives to={href} unless to is passed explicitly.

name: useLinkify
summary: Finds URLs, email addresses and custom patterns in plain text and returns React nodes with a Link for each match; the links respect LinkProvider for client-side routing. Use it wherever user- or tool-authored plain text should grow safe, styled links without pre-parsing it into markup: activity feeds, comment threads, description fields. Custom patterns turn project-specific references (issue numbers like #123, ticket IDs) into links by supplying a regex plus an href builder — e.g. an issue tracker pattern that maps captures onto its URL scheme. When matches overlap, the earliest one wins, and at the same start a custom pattern wins over the built-in ones, so a custom #123 pattern coexists with URL detection in the same string.

name: useListFocus
summary: Manages keyboard navigation within a linear list following WAI-ARIA menu/listbox/toolbar patterns. Supports arrow key navigation (vertical, horizontal, or both), Home/End for boundaries, optional wrap-around, RTL, and Escape to close. Opt into hasRovingTabIndex for composite widgets (toolbars, segmented controls, tab strips) that own a single tab stop. Suitable for dropdown menus, toolbars, and any 1D focusable list.

name: useLocale
summary: Reads the authoritative Astryx locale. Use it to thread the provider locale into pure formatting helpers and sibling-package APIs; do not derive a second locale from navigator.language or a hardcoded literal.

name: useLongPress
summary: Detects a single-finger press-and-hold and reports where it happened, so touch users can reach affordances that a pointer gets from right-click. iOS Safari never synthesizes a contextmenu event on long-press, which makes this the only touch route into a cursor-positioned surface such as ContextMenu. The press cancels on movement, lift, multi-touch or unmount. The hold is timed on the touch events’ own timestamps: when a busy page handles the lift late, a finger held for the full delay still reports its long press, before the lift acts.

name: useMediaQuery
summary: SSR-safe media query hook that subscribes to window.matchMedia changes. Returns whether the given media query matches. Always returns false on first render for SSR compatibility. Where `window.matchMedia` is missing, it returns its server default and never throws.

name: useMenuPress
summary: The press model of macOS and iOS menus, for any pointer: the row under the pointer when it is RELEASED is the row that acts, the highlight follows the pointer while it is held, a mouse opens the menu on press and can drag straight into it, and a finger or a pen opens it while still down: as it presses with no delay given, picking a row only after moving 10 px, or else once it is held for the delay. The pointer is tracked at document level by pointerId, so a finger that slid off the row it landed on is still followed; the click the browser reports at the end of a touch, aimed at the row where the touch began, is swallowed so nothing acts twice. DropdownMenu, ContextMenu, DropdownMenuSubMenu, Selector and the menu bottom sheet already mount it; reach for it directly only when building a menu-like surface of your own.

name: useMergedRefs
summary: Combines multiple object or callback refs into one stable callback ref. Use it when a component must forward a consumer ref while also attaching internal refs. Unlike calling mergeRefs during render, the callback identity stays stable across unrelated rerenders, so React does not detach and reattach the element.

name: useMultiCombobox
summary: Tracks the active option of a multi-select combobox and handles its keys, while DOM focus stays on the control. It powers MultiSelector; unlike useCombobox, toggling an option keeps the list open, and rows can carry an action cell. It renders nothing and sets no attributes: the caller renders the control and the list, and wires the ARIA attributes from what it returns.

name: useOutlineFromDOM
summary: Builds outline items from the headings already in the page. Use it when the article is not a Markdown string, and pass the items to Outline. The list updates when headings are added, removed, renamed, or given a new id. A null ref returns an empty list.

name: useOutlineFromMarkdown
summary: Extracts the headings of a Markdown string for an Outline next to the rendered document. It uses the parser and heading slugs that Markdown uses, so in a complete document each item links to its heading, and fenced code never counts as a heading. The result is memoized on the source and the options. Outside React, use parseOutlineFromMarkdown.

name: useOverflow
summary: Measures children rendered in a hidden container to determine how many fit in the available width without flickering. Uses ResizeObserver to react to container and measured-child size changes. The measurement container should hold all items plus an optional overflow indicator element (identified by a data-overflow-indicator attribute).

name: useOverlay
summary: Adds overlay behavior to a container you already render, such as a Card or a custom media frame, without the wrapper Overlay adds. Spread containerRef and containerProps on the container, then render element (or renderOverlay(children)) once inside it. The scrim is absolutely positioned, so it covers the nearest positioned ancestor: the container itself, or a positioned section inside it such as an image area. Visibility is CSS-driven from the container's :hover and :focus-within, so with showOn 'hover' a keyboard user reveals the content by moving focus into the container. On a device with a mouse or trackpad, content that a hover or focus reveal hides stays in the tab order, so Tab reaches an action in it and focus reveals the scrim. On a touch-primary device a hover overlay stays inert until a tap. A revealed scrim takes pointer input over the area it covers, so keep any other control in the container outside the scrim, or use a top or bottom strip and keep the control in the part the strip leaves uncovered.

name: usePanGesture
summary: Reports a drag on an element as values, for a surface the product moves itself: a card that follows the finger, a drawer pulled by its handle. A finger, a mouse and a pen all drive it. A mouse or pen drag that starts on selectable text selects that text, and the pan reports nothing. Give that text `user-select: none`. The drag claims its touch at UIKit’s 10 pt, as `UIPanGestureRecognizer` does, so a tap stays a tap, and a press or a long press is never reported as a pan. With `axis`, a scroll across that axis that starts on the element stays the page’s; without it, the pan takes a drag in any direction, so a finger’s scroll that starts on the element moves the element instead of the page. A trackpad scroll still scrolls the page. The hook is a thin layer over `createPanGesture`, the same API for code without React. A drag has no keyboard or assistive-technology path of its own: whatever the drag does needs another way to do it, such as buttons or arrow keys (WCAG 2.5.7). The pan moves nothing itself, so Reduce Motion applies to the motion you drive from it: honor the user’s reduced-motion setting in the animation that moves the element. Where a component already offers the behavior, use its prop instead: BottomSheet’s `snapPoints`, Carousel’s `hasSnap`.

name: usePopover
summary: Headless hook for click-triggered popovers with focus trapping. Combines useLayer with useFocusTrap, auto-focus, light dismiss, Escape handling, and an optional hidden close button for accessible dialog-like popover behavior. Every painted surface emits the canonical popover target. A custom composition needing a distinct stable seam should pass and document its own surfaceTarget.

name: usePowerSearchConfig
summary: Memoizes a PowerSearch configuration built from typed field definitions and returns it along with an applyFilters function for client-side filtering. Automatically maps field types (string, number, boolean, date, enum, etc.) to their canonical operators and provides an efficient predicate evaluator to filter datasets.

name: usePressFeedback
summary: The touch press model every Astryx pressable uses, for a local component that paints its own press. Under a finger, CSS `:active` paints on the touch itself and can outlive the start of a scroll; the press model instead tracks the touch the way UIKit tracks a control: it highlights as the finger lands (after the content-touch delay inside a scroller, where a flick paints nothing), a quick tap answers at the lift, and a scroll that takes the touch cancels it with no fade. One document-level controller does this for every marked element (installed by the first pressable to mount, removed by the last to unmount), so calling the hook adds no listener or state to your element. On a desktop a mouse press is still your `:active` rule: keep it, and drop it under `@media (pointer: coarse)` the way the built-in components do. That query reads the primary pointer, so on a phone or tablet it also drops `:active` for a connected mouse, trackpad or keyboard; the controller paints those presses there (at once, faded at the release), so nothing goes unanswered.

name: useResizable
summary: Hook for adding drag-to-resize behavior to layout regions. Supports single-region and multi-region configurations with snap points, collapsible panels, localStorage persistence, and cascade resize ordering.

name: useScrollableArea
summary: Adds canonical axis-aware scroll behavior to structure owned by the caller. An axis is effective only when its computed overflow is scroll-capable and geometry exceeds the shared 1px tolerance. Both viewport and content boxes are observed.

name: useScrollLock
summary: Locks page scroll while active and keeps the page where it is. The page gets overflow: hidden (on the root, or on body when its own overflow is the one the viewport uses), which stops wheel, keyboard and scrollbar scrolling, and overscroll-behavior-y: none on the root and body, which stops the overscroll bounce while the lock holds. Where the primary pointer is coarse (phones and tablets), a one-finger pan that would scroll the page is cancelled, because iOS Safari scrolls an overflow: hidden page under a finger; pans that a scroller inside the overlay can take, drags on a native range input, pinch-zoom, and one-finger drags on a pinch-zoomed page (which pan the zoomed view) still work. The scroll offset never changes, so nothing jumps when the lock starts or ends, and iOS Safari keeps its toolbar as it was. Where the hidden scrollbar takes layout space (desktop), the hook holds its gutter open with scrollbar-gutter: stable, so the page, including any position: fixed chrome, does not shift sideways.

name: useScrollOverflow
summary: Tracks scroll overflow state for a horizontally scrollable container. Returns a ref callback and state booleans that update as the user scrolls, the container resizes, or its content changes (a child added, removed or resized, or a new gap or padding). Uses scroll event listeners, ResizeObserver and MutationObserver for reactive updates. Tolerance of 1px is applied to avoid sub-pixel false positives.

name: useSnapPaging
summary: Gives a Carousel iOS paging on native snap's stops: pass the value as hasSnap={useSnapPaging()}. Under a finger and on a trackpad swipe, a flick moves one view, or one item with {pages: 'item'}, and the row rests on an item's start edge. A mouse wheel keeps native snapping. Only a carousel given the value loads the paging code.

name: useSpeechRecognition
summary: A headless speech-recognition control. It does not write into a composer. Read the transcript from interimTranscript and onResult, and draw your own UI from isListening and volume. Check isSupported first. useChatDictation adds composer interim text and start and stop cues on top of this hook.

name: useStreamingText
summary: Smooths bursty streamed text into a steady character-by-character reveal using requestAnimationFrame. Decouples arrival rate from display rate. Advances on word and syntax boundaries to avoid slicing mid-markdown or mid-word, preventing visual glitches with markdown renderers. Animation timing derives from Astryx motion tokens via useTheme when available, with sensible fallbacks outside a theme provider. Snaps to full text when isStreaming becomes false.

name: useSyntaxTheme
summary: Reads syntax colors for a canvas or other drawing that cannot use the CSS variables SyntaxTheme sets. Call it under a SyntaxTheme. It returns null when that provider is absent, so the caller can skip drawing.

name: useTableColumnResize
summary: Hook that returns a TablePlugin adding draggable resize handles to column header borders. T is the row type; TypeScript cannot infer it from the config, so it defaults to Record<string, unknown>, which a Table with typed rows rejects: pass it, as in `useTableColumnResize<Walk>(…)` for `<Table<Walk>>`. Supports pointer + keyboard (WAI-ARIA window splitter) resizing, RTL, per-column min/max widths, and proportional-column preservation (resizes the neighbor so the table stays full-width). Commits widths on release.

name: useTableColumnSettings
summary: Headless column visibility and ordering management for Table. T is the row type; TypeScript cannot infer it from the config, so it defaults to Record<string, unknown>, which a Table with typed rows rejects: pass it, as in `useTableColumnSettings<Walk>(…)` for `<Table<Walk>>`. When the column keys have a narrower type than string (a union, or keys that useTableColumnSettingsState infers from its columns), pass both: `useTableColumnSettings<Walk, WalkColumnKey>(…)`. Provides filtered columns, toggle helpers, and pre-built MultiSelector options for a column picker UI.

name: useTableColumnSettingsState
summary: Headless column visibility and ordering state management for Table. Manages which columns are active, provides toggle and reset operations, and produces a config object that feeds directly into useTableColumnSettings. Renderer-agnostic and pairs with any column picker UI.

name: useTableColumnsVirtualization
summary: Returns an opaque capability for Table column windowing. Pass the capability to Table.virtualization and keep the complete data, columns, explicit stable idKey and plugins on Table. Columns keep their declared widths: an overflowing Table renders at its minimum width, and the window uses the width each column has there. Pinned columns from useTableStickyColumns always mount; only the columns between the pinned runs window, with a few overscan columns on each side. When the Table's scroll area is at least as wide as the Table's minimum width, every column mounts. A focused cell keeps its column mounted while it scrolls out of view, until focus leaves the Table or moves to another cell. Changing column order, widths, visibility or pinning keeps the first visible column and its scroll offset. Supported tables have one header row, flat rows, no cell that spans columns and single-line content; explicit wrapping, arbitrary custom renderers, non-flat rows, invalid identity, a caller-provided scrollWrapper or a min-width wider than the column floors render every column. To window rows and columns together, pass both capabilities as a list: Table.virtualization={[rows, columns]}. Mounted cells keep native table semantics and full-table column positions; unmounted columns are not promised screen-reader discovery. Keep the capability on the Table for its whole life: adding or removing it remounts the table, which resets focus and scroll position. Changing initialViewportWidth does not remount it.

name: useTableFiltering
summary: Table plugin that adds inline column filters with popover or inline controls. T is the row type; TypeScript cannot infer it from the config, so it defaults to Record<string, unknown>, which a Table with typed rows rejects: pass it, as in `useTableFiltering<Walk>(…)` for `<Table<Walk>>`. Pairs with useTableFilterState for managed state. Supports text, select, multi-select, date, and number filter types via PowerSearch field definitions. The plugin renders the filter controls only; it does not remove rows. Filter the data yourself (toSearchFilters with applyFilters from usePowerSearchConfig) and pass the result to Table. When no row matches, Table shows its emptyState prop.

name: useTableFilterState
summary: Managed state hook for table filtering. Returns filters (the current filter map), onFilterChange, and clearAll (clears every filter, for example from a "Clear filters" button in the Table emptyState). Pass filters and onFilterChange to useTableFiltering.

name: useTableGroupedRows
summary: Hook that groups a flat data array into collapsible section rows. Each distinct groupBy value becomes a full-width section-header row with a chevron toggle, the group label, and a member count; collapsing hides that group's data rows while keeping the header visible. The disclosure state lives on the chevron button, not the native table row. Mirrors useTableTreeState: the consumer owns the collapsedGroups set and the hook returns {data, plugin, idKey}: pass them to Table as data, plugins, and idKey respectively. Grouping runs on the rows you hand it, so with pagination the order is filter, sort, slice, then group: sort by the group key first and the user's keys second, so a section's rows stay contiguous and each page appends to the bottom of the table instead of splicing rows in above the reader. A page that ends on a row count still cuts mid-section, and the heading then counts what has loaded rather than what exists: "6" quietly becoming "10". Where the full result set is in hand, carry the cut forward to the end of the section it lands in: every rendered section is then whole and its count is a total.

name: useTableInfiniteScroll
summary: Call useTableInfiniteScroll<T>({hasMore, isLoading, onLoadMore}) and pass the result to <Table plugins={{infiniteScroll: plugin}} />. T is the row type; TypeScript cannot infer it from the config, so it defaults to Record<string, unknown>, which a Table with typed rows rejects: pass it, as in `useTableInfiniteScroll<Walk>(…)` for `<Table<Walk>>`. Keep accumulated rows in your own state. onLoadMore must return a Promise<void> that settles when the batch work completes. A fulfilled request finishes after settlement and a subsequent committed isLoading=false; a true loading phase is not required. Visible short batches can automatically request again in a later task, so update hasMore when the source is exhausted. A resolved request that appends no rows must not incorrectly claim endless more data. Throws, rejections and invalid non-Promise results pause automatic loading; the manual Button can retry once controlled loading is false. The hook does not render product errors or cancel transport. For a new dataset, key and remount the component owning both the hook and its Table, not only the Table child; prevent stale responses from committing caller data yourself. Children mode and unsupported row models do not load and emit a deduplicated development warning. Body modifiers must declare compatible rowModel: flat. Observation uses the Table scroll area while the Table windows its rows, and the browser viewport otherwise, with zero look-ahead and no ancestor discovery. Without IntersectionObserver, the same manual command works.

name: useTablePagination
summary: Call useTablePagination with a config object containing page state and callback. T is the row type; TypeScript cannot infer it from the config, so it defaults to Record<string, unknown>, which a Table with typed rows rejects: pass it, as in `useTablePagination<Walk>(…)` for `<Table<Walk>>`. Pass the returned plugin to Table via the plugins prop.

name: useTableRowExpansion
summary: Hook that returns a TablePlugin which expands a full-width detail panel below a row, rendered by the consumer via renderExpanded(item). Adds a leading chevron column and a right-click "Expand/Collapse row" action; the consumer owns the expandedKeys set. The panel spans the row but starts its content at the first column, past the chevron, so detail lines up with the labels above it; the inset follows the table density. Use it for master-detail rows (order details, forms, charts, nested tables). For hierarchical data where child rows reuse the parent columns, use useTableTreeData + useTableTreeState instead.

name: useTableRowIndex
summary: Hook that returns a TablePlugin which prepends a right-aligned, monospaced row-number column, starting at 1 by default. Without data, Table supplies row positions; with data, ordinary numbers follow that array. Windowed rows use the parent Table logical position directly; nondefault startFrom values use full rendering.

name: useTableRowStatus
summary: Hook that returns a TablePlugin which prepends a narrow column signaling per-row status. Return {status, label} for a semantic success, warning, or error: Table resolves the matching glyph and tone through the active theme. Return {color, icon?, label} for a custom marker: every color is paint-only, an omitted icon renders the stable 8px dot, and an explicit icon renders that caller-selected glyph. Named custom icons keep their released Icon color mapping; raw CSS custom icons inherit the caller's exact paint instead of the previous primary fallback. Existing callers require no source migration. label is required and becomes the accessible image name plus supplemental hover tooltip; return null for no indicator. The column header is visually blank but carries a screen-reader-only localized name ("Row status", i18n key @astryx.table.rowStatus.columnHeader). Memoize getStatus with useCallback for a stable plugin identity.

name: useTableRowsVirtualization
summary: Returns an opaque capability for fixed-height flat-row Table windowing. Pass the capability to Table.virtualization and keep the complete data, columns, explicit stable idKey and plugins on Table. Sizes are positive finite CSS pixels. The Table scrolls inside the height its parent gives it and fills all of it. Give the Table's parent a height, fixed or relative, or a flex child, so windowing can bound the rows; with no height every row renders. Make the Table the parent's only child, or a flex child with min-height: 0 beside a heading or toolbar. Supported rows use single-line content; explicit wrapping, non-flat rows or invalid identity use ordinary full rendering. What stays windowed: a column without renderCell (its default cell renders the row's value as single-line text) and the row-number (useTableRowIndex, counting from 1) and selection (useTableSelection) columns. A column with a custom renderCell turns windowing off for the whole table, because Table cannot check that the cell keeps the fixed row height; it renders every row and warns in development, naming the column. A useTableRowStatus column, or a useTableRowIndex column that counts from another number, turns windowing off too. To window a table, put the text a column shows in the row data and leave renderCell off that column. Windowing uses the Table-owned scroll wrapper; a caller-provided scrollWrapper takes diagnostic full-render fallback. Mounted rows retain native table semantics and full-table positions; unmounted rows are not promised screen-reader discovery.

name: useTableSelection
summary: Hook that returns a TablePlugin implementing row selection with checkboxes, select-all, and aria-selected. Uses React Context for independent checkbox re-renders.

name: useTableSelectionState
summary: State management companion for useTableSelection that returns {selectionConfig, selectionState}: selectionConfig (UseTableSelectionConfig<T>) goes to useTableSelection, and selectionState (TableSelectionState) has selectedKeys: ReadonlySet<string>, selectedCount: number, hasSelection: boolean, and clearSelection: () => void, for a bulk-action bar such as TableSelectionToolbar. selectedKeys holds the complete selection, also keys outside the current view, and clearSelection clears all of them. Handles disabled/selectable row filtering for select-all automatically: disabled rows are frozen (preserved across select-all/deselect-all), non-selectable rows are excluded.

name: useTableSortable
summary: useTableSortable adds the header sort controls but does not reorder the rows: pass rows that are already sorted as data, sorted by you from the sort state or by useTableSortableState. T is the row type; TypeScript cannot infer it from the config, so it defaults to Record<string, unknown>, which a Table with typed rows rejects: pass it, as in `useTableSortable<Walk>(…)` for `<Table<Walk>>`. When the sort keys have a narrower type than string (a union, or keys that useTableSortableState infers from defaultSort), pass both: `useTableSortable<Walk, WalkSortKey>(…)`. Call it with a config object containing the sort state and callback, and pass the returned plugin to Table via the plugins prop.

name: useTableSortableState
summary: Owns a Table's sort state and sorts the rows locally, as a convenience layer over useTableSortable. Pass the rows in, render sortedData, and hand sortConfig to useTableSortable. The hook keeps the state (or reads it from sort and onSortChange when controlled), so header clicks re-sort the rows with no sort code in the component. With isMultiSortEnabled, Shift+click adds tiebreaker columns. For data sorted on a server, use useTableSortable directly and sort where the data lives.

name: useTableStickyColumns
summary: Hook that returns a TablePlugin which pins a contiguous run of columns to the start and/or end edge of the table. T is the row type; TypeScript cannot infer it from the config, so it defaults to Record<string, unknown>, which a Table with typed rows rejects: pass it, as in `useTableStickyColumns<Walk>(…)` for `<Table<Walk>>`. Pinned columns get cumulative offsets and a soft, scroll-aware shadow over the scrolling content. An empty config ({}) is a valid no-op that pins nothing.

name: useTableTreeData
summary: Headless tree plugin for Table: renders nested rows with per-level indentation and expand/collapse chevrons in the tree column (the first column by default), and follows the disclosure pattern: each expand/collapse button carries aria-expanded and, while expanded, aria-controls naming its child rows; indentation shows the hierarchy visually. Composable with the other Table plugins: the canonical plugin order places tree before selection, so the checkbox column lands left of the indented tree column. Feed it the treeConfig from useTableTreeState, or construct the config directly for server-driven or pre-flattened trees. When no row is expandable (flat data), every transform is a pass-through and the table renders identically to one without the plugin. Known limitation: the tree column wraps its cell content, so textOverflow="truncate" tooltips do not apply within the tree column.

name: useTableTreeState
summary: State management companion for useTableTreeData. Owns the expanded set (controlled or uncontrolled) and flattens nested data into the visible row array; collapsed subtrees are unmounted, not hidden, so the table body contains exactly the visible rows. Returns expandAll/collapseAll helpers, the aggregate isAllExpanded state (true/false/indeterminate) for a header expand-all control, and a ready-to-use config for the tree plugin. Note: because collapsed rows unmount, cell-local React state inside collapsed subtrees is lost on collapse; lift state that must survive.

name: useTheme
summary: Programmatic access to theme tokens for non-CSS consumers like SVG, canvas, Vega, D3, maps, or chart libraries that need values in JavaScript instead of CSS custom property references.

name: useThemeName
summary: Reads only the active theme name. Use it when code needs to know which theme is on, and does not need tokens or the color mode. It reads ThemeContext when a Theme is above the caller, and otherwise the root theme name on the document element.

name: useToast
summary: Hook for showing toast notifications from anywhere in your component tree; it needs no provider or mounted ToastViewport: inside LayerProvider (or a ToastViewport) it uses that viewport, and otherwise the first toast mounts a fallback viewport on document.body with a development warning. Returns the show function itself (not an object): `const showToast = useToast()`; call it with toast options to show the notification.

name: useTooltip
summary: Headless hook for hover/focus-triggered tooltips. Builds on useLayer with hover intent, keyboard focus handling, and accessible aria-describedby linking. Use for custom trigger elements that need tooltip behavior without the wrapper component.

name: useTranslator
summary: Returns a translator function that resolves keys against the current locale, provider overrides, and the shipped English fallback catalog. Call inside a component; the returned function can be used anywhere within that component's scope.

name: useTreeFocus
summary: Manages roving-tabindex focus and the WAI-ARIA tree keyboard model. ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Home/End roam linearly over the visible treeitems (skipping disabled ones), while ArrowRight/ArrowLeft carry tree semantics (expand/collapse, move to first-child/parent). Enter/Space activate, and printable characters trigger typeahead.

name: useTruncation
summary: Detects whether an element's text is cut off — single-line overflow or clamped to several lines — and gives back the full text, updating when the size or the content changes. Built on a shared ResizeObserver and a shared MutationObserver, so hundreds of table cells create one observer of each kind, and a first measurement runs batched in a microtask after the commit instead of forcing a layout pass per text during mount. Use it wherever a truncated cell should show its full content only when it is actually truncated: compose a Tooltip off isTruncated and fullText instead of always rendering one. Text and Heading build their truncation tooltips on it; reach for it directly when composing truncation feedback into your own component.

name: useTypeahead
summary: Adds APG type-to-focus search to a collection: printable keystrokes are buffered (resetting after a pause), and the first item whose label starts with the buffer (ignoring case, accents, the stroked letters đ ł ø ħ ŧ ƀ and Turkish ı/İ, the same in every locale; a typed accent prefers the exact match) is reported through onMatch. Pressing the same letter repeatedly cycles through the matches rather than filtering deeper. It moves nothing itself; pair it with the collection's own focus management, most often useListFocus or useGridFocus.

name: VisuallyHidden
summary: Renders content in the accessibility tree while hiding it visually. Use for accessible names on icon-only controls, aria-live announcement regions, and supplementary screen-reader context. Deliberately has no styling props; the whole point is to stay invisible. `xstyle` is still accepted and ignored, only so code written against 0.7.2 keeps compiling; a planned minor removes it.
